issues.legal_issue: An official communication that clearly informs an interested person that an award has been made and the person's claim has been rejected is sufficient notice to start the limitation period for seeking a reference.
material_facts: The land acquisition officer sent a telegram informing the claimant that the award had been declared and that the claimant's demand had been rejected.
The claimant received the telegram but filed the reference application more than six weeks later.
The award had considered and rejected the claimant's claim for compensation.
issues.conclusion: The telegram was sufficient notice of the award, and the reference application, filed more than six weeks after its receipt, was barred by limitation.
issues.legal_principle: Under Sections 12(2) and 18(2)(b) of the Land Acquisition Act, notice need only clearly intimate that the award has been made; it need not set out the award's details or follow a prescribed form. The six-week period runs from receipt of such notice. State of Punjab v. Satinder Bir Singh (1995) holds that notice is an intimation of the award and that limitation does not depend on communication in any particular form where none is prescribed. The rule in Raja Harish Chandra Raj Singh v. Deputy Land Acquisition Officer, which the Court said would otherwise merit consideration regarding knowledge of an award, did not govern because notice under Section 12(2) had been received.

predicates.land_acquisition_reference_proceeding: A person sought a court reference concerning compensation in a land acquisition proceeding.
predicates.official_award_communication_received: The interested person received an official communication from the acquisition authority about the award.
predicates.communication_identified_award_and_rejec: The communication stated that the award had been made and that the person's claim had been rejected.
predicates.reference_application_filed_after_six_we: The person filed the reference application more than six weeks after receiving the communication.

issues.definition: When an interested person in a land acquisition reference proceeding receives an official communication identifying the award and rejection of the claim, filing the reference application more than six weeks later makes the application barred by limitation.

issues.legal_issue: A decision that considers a compensation claim and rejects it is an award even if no compensation is granted to the claimant.
material_facts: The acquisition officer considered the claimant's claim for compensation.
The officer rejected the claim on the ground that the claimant held leasehold rights and was not entitled to compensation, which was awarded to the landowners instead.
issues.conclusion: The rejection of the claimant's compensation claim constituted an award, commonly described as a nil award, despite the claimant receiving no compensation.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 11 and 18 of the Land Acquisition Act treat an acquisition officer's decision on a compensation claim as an award from which an interested person may seek a reference. A total rejection of a claim is an award even though no compensation is calculated or granted to that claimant. No earlier case was cited for this proposition.

predicates.land_acquisition_compensation_proceeding: An acquisition authority determined compensation arising from the taking of land.
predicates.claimant_compensation_claim_considered: The authority considered the claimant's request for compensation.
predicates.claimant_compensation_claim_rejected: The authority rejected the claimant's request for compensation.

issues.definition: In a land acquisition compensation proceeding, a considered and rejected compensation claim counts as an award.

issues.legal_issue: A court or acquisition officer dealing with a reference application has no power to condone delay in filing it.
material_facts: The reference application was filed outside the applicable six-week period after the claimant received notice of the award.
The State challenged the reference as late, and the absence of a power to condone delay was not disputed before the Court.
issues.conclusion: The delay in making the reference application could not be condoned by the acquisition officer or the court considering the reference.
issues.legal_principle: The Court applied the limitation requirements in Section 18(2) of the Land Acquisition Act and noted that neither the acquisition officer making a reference nor the court considering one has power to condone delay in making the application. This absence of power was not disputed before the Court.

predicates.land_acquisition_reference_proceeding: A person sought a court reference concerning compensation in a land acquisition proceeding.
predicates.reference_application_filed_after_applic: The person filed the reference application after the applicable time limit had expired.

issues.definition: When a reference application in a land acquisition proceeding is filed after the applicable time limit, the delay cannot be condoned.
